meta: Does AI learn something every time you ask it a question? No. Bit explains the two stages: training, when a model learns once at huge cost, and inference, when it answers you.

muc.title: Does AI learn from my questions?
muc.text: Mark thinks that every time he asks a question, AI learns a little more from it.

muc.title: Training: learn once, at great cost
muc.text: Bit explains: there are two stages. Training is when the model learns, running on tens of thousands of GPUs for months and costing a fortune. Once it's done, the knowledge in the model is frozen.

muc.title: Inference: every time you ask
muc.text: Inference is when the model uses that knowledge to answer you. Each question takes just a few seconds of computing, and the model doesn't change itself.

muc.title: Like school and then work
muc.text: It's like four years of university being training, and answering customers every day at work being inference.

muc.title: So how does AI remember me?
muc.text: AI remembers your name thanks to the Memory feature, notes sent along with each question, as in videos 9 and 27. The model isn't learning again.

muc.title: It can run on your home computer
muc.text: Knowing this shows you: training needs a whole data center, but inference for a small model can run right on your laptop.

muc.title: Ask AI about its knowledge cutoff
muc.text: Ask the AI you use how up to date its knowledge is. That's exactly when its training ended.
